guide.title: Getting started
guide.intro: Everything you need to put your WhatsApp to work. No code required. In ten minutes you'll connect your number, organize your inbox, and leave the automation running.

connect.title: 1. Connect your number
paragraphs: In WhatsApp Sessions, create a session, name it (say "Sales") and scan the QR code from the phone that owns the number: WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices → Link a device.
That's it: messages to that number appear in your inbox, and the phone keeps working as usual. Connect more numbers depending on your plan.
items: Tip: turn on "Save contacts automatically" on the session so everyone who writes in gets recorded in Contacts.

inbox.title: 2. The message inbox
paragraphs: Messages holds every conversation: reply with text or files, leave internal notes (never sent to the customer) and mark conversations resolved.
Work it as a team: assign each conversation to an owner, tag it with colors, and filter by status, assignee or tag.
items: Quick replies: save a sent message from its ⋯ bubble menu and reuse it with the composer's ⚡ button.
Tags: create them on the fly from a chat or manage them in their own section.

contacts.title: 3. Contacts
paragraphs: Contacts is your address book: WhatsApp name and number, plus company, email, website, Instagram and notes. It fills itself if you enable auto-save on a session, or from a flow via the "Save contact" node.
Each contact shows which of your numbers they've written to. Useful when sales and support run on separate lines.

aiAgents.title: 4. AI agents
paragraphs: An AI agent replies for you in your own voice: define its character and instructions, upload reference documents, and use your own Anthropic or OpenAI key. You control the model cost.
Assign it to a session and it answers inbound messages. It can pause itself and alert you when a conversation needs a human, and you can pause or resume it per conversation from the inbox.
items: On Pro and Business, agents can also use MCP tools to query your own systems.

humanAgents.title: 5. Human agents & mirror groups
paragraphs: A human agent is a real person answering from their own WhatsApp. No account or password needed: just their number.

When a lead is handed to a human, whathooks creates a mirror group on WhatsApp with that person. Everything the lead writes appears in the group, and whatever the agent replies reaches the lead as your brand. The lead never sees the agent's personal number.
items: Link a human agent to a team member so handoffs also assign the conversation to them in the inbox.

flows.title: 6. Flows (beta)
paragraphs: Flows is your visual router: it decides what happens to every inbound message. Connect nodes for keywords, AI intent classification, agent replies, human handoff (one person, round-robin, or a shared team group), tags, contacts and webhooks.
Start from a template, assign it a session and enable it. The Runs panel shows the path each message took, so you tune without guessing.
items: Tip: check "Copy the conversation history" on handoff nodes so the human gets the full context when the group opens.

team.title: 7. Your team & roles
paragraphs: Invite your team from the Team section. Roles define what each person sees: Admin manages everything; Member works the inbox (optionally limited to certain sessions); Operator only sees the conversations you assign to them. Ideal for support staff.

docs.title: whathooks documentation
docs.subtitle: Connect a WhatsApp number, receive inbound messages on your webhook, and send replies through our REST API.
docs.introP1: whathooks lets your clients connect their own WhatsApp number by scanning a QR code. Once linked, the integration works in two directions:
docs.introInbound: <hl>Inbound → webhook.</hl> Every message your number receives is POSTed as JSON to a webhook URL you configure.
docs.introOutbound: <hl>Outbound → API.</hl> You send replies by calling our REST API at <pill>/v1</pill>.
docs.introP2: Your number is connected through a WhatsApp Web link, the same mechanism as WhatsApp's “linked devices”. Reconnection after a dropped link is handled automatically, and each number supports one linked device.
docs.introNote: Because this uses an unofficial WhatsApp Web connection, treat it like a linked device: keep the phone reachable and avoid behavior that could get the number flagged by WhatsApp.
docs.quickstartIntro: Get from zero to a sent message in four steps.
docs.qs1Desc: Sign up and create an organization. All sessions, webhooks, and API keys live under your organization.
docs.qs2Title: 2. Create a WhatsApp session & scan the QR
docs.qs2Desc: Create a session in the dashboard, then open WhatsApp on your phone → <pill>Linked Devices</pill> → <pill>Link a Device</pill> and scan the QR.
docs.qs3Desc: Register an HTTPS endpoint to receive <pill>message.received</pill> and session events.
docs.qs4Desc: Generate an API key to send messages programmatically via <pill>POST /v1/messages</pill>.
docs.connectingIntro: A session moves through a series of statuses as it links and stays online. You can poll a session or subscribe to <pill>session.status</pill> webhooks to track it.

statuses.QR: A QR code is ready to be scanned with WhatsApp.
statuses.CONNECTED: Online and ready to send and receive messages.
statuses.DISCONNECTED: Connection dropped; reconnection is attempted automatically.
statuses.LOGGED_OUT: The device was unlinked; a new QR scan is required.

docs.embedTitle: Embed the QR in your product
docs.embedDesc: Sessions are fully manageable with an API key, so your product can onboard users without ever showing them the whathooks dashboard: create a session, then render the pairing QR in your own UI. <pill>GET /v1/sessions/:id</pill> returns <pill>qrDataUrl</pill>. A ready-to-embed PNG data URI (<imgtag></imgtag>). QR codes rotate, so poll the session while it's in the <pill>QR</pill> status or subscribe to <pill>session.qr</pill> webhooks for fresh codes, and watch for <pill>CONNECTED</pill> to dismiss the QR.
docs.webhooksIntro: When something happens on a session, we POST a JSON body to your configured webhook URL.

events.messageReceived: An inbound WhatsApp message arrived on a connected session.
events.sessionStatus: A session changed status (e.g. CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, LOGGED_OUT).
events.contactCreated: A new contact was saved. Via the session's auto-save setting, a flow's "Save contact" node, or manual creation.
events.contactUpdated: An existing contact changed: fields edited, name backfilled from WhatsApp, or a new session linked.
events.sessionQr: A new QR code was generated and is waiting to be scanned.

docs.headersIntro: Every delivery includes these request headers:

headers.signature: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, formatted as sha256=<hex>.
headers.delivery: A unique ID for this delivery attempt.

docs.envelopeDesc: Every delivery body shares the same envelope: <envtag></envtag>. Below is a full <pill>message.received</pill> delivery:
docs.customizeDesc: Optionally give a webhook mapping rules to reshape data to match your system: rename fields, format dates, and inject fixed values. When rules are set, data contains only the fields you map. The envelope stays the same. Each rule has a target (output name) and either a source (dot path like data.from, also reaching event, sessionId, timestamp) or a fixed value. Add dateFormat to a source rule to format it as a date: iso, unix, unix_ms, or a UTC pattern using yyyy MM dd HH mm ss. Configure it on the webhook in the dashboard, or pass payloadMapping when creating one via API.
docs.signatureDesc: Verify each delivery by computing an HMAC-SHA256 of the <hl>raw</hl> request body using your webhook secret, then comparing it to the <pill>X-Whathooks-Signature</pill> header. Always compare with a constant-time function.
docs.sendingIntro: Send a message with <pill>POST /v1/messages</pill>, authenticated with an API key via the <apikeytag></apikeytag> header. An <bearertag></bearertag> header also works.
docs.sendingTo: The <pill>to</pill> field accepts a bare phone number (digits only, with country code, no <pill>+</pill>) or a full WhatsApp JID. The target session must be <pill>CONNECTED</pill> or the request returns <pill>400</pill>.
docs.sendingSuccess: A successful request responds with the queued message:
docs.apiRefIntro: Base URL in production: <pill>https://api.whathooks.com/v1</pill>. Dashboard requests use a <hl>JWT</hl> (from <pill>/v1/auth/login</pill>), while programmatic requests use an <hl>API key</hl>.
docs.err401: Missing or invalid credentials (JWT or API key).
docs.err400: The session is not <pill>CONNECTED</pill>, or the request body is invalid.
docs.errWebhooks: Delivery requests time out after 10 seconds. For now we make a single delivery attempt per event. Automatic retries are coming.
docs.agentsCallout: Building with an AI coding agent? Give it the whole API in one markdown file: <link>whathooks.app/llms.txt</link>
docs.payloadNotes: <pill>type</pill> is uppercase (<pill>TEXT</pill>, <pill>IMAGE</pill>, <pill>AUDIO</pill>, <pill>VIDEO</pill>, <pill>DOCUMENT</pill>, <pill>STICKER</pill>, <pill>LOCATION</pill>, <pill>CONTACT</pill>, <pill>UNKNOWN</pill>). <pill>data.timestamp</pill> is unix seconds (the WhatsApp message time); the envelope <pill>timestamp</pill> is the ISO delivery time.
docs.mediaDesc: For media messages, <pill>media</pill> carries a signed download link (expires after 1 hour. Download promptly, or re-fetch the message via <pill>GET /v1/messages</pill> for a fresh link). <pill>text</pill> holds the caption, if any:

meta.title: whathooks for teams. One WhatsApp inbox for everyone
meta.description: Put your whole team behind one WhatsApp number. A shared inbox with full history, roles, and real-time replies from the dashboard. No code required.

teams.heroSubtitle: Your business WhatsApp shouldn't live in someone's pocket. Connect your number once and let support, sales, and ops answer from a shared inbox. Same number, full history, real time.
teams.heroNote: 7-day free trial · No Business API approval · Cancel anytime

teams.painsSubtitle: Every team running WhatsApp from one phone knows these.

pains.title: The phone is the bottleneck
pains.desc: Whoever holds the handset is customer service today. Everyone else forwards, waits, or interrupts.

pains.title: Screenshots as a workflow
pains.desc: A customer writes in, someone screenshots it to the sales group, three people debate, nobody replies.

pains.title: History walks out the door
pains.desc: When the WhatsApp lives on a personal phone, every conversation leaves with the employee who owned it.

teams.afterSubtitle: Everyone sees every conversation. Anyone can pick up any chat, right where it left off.

after.title: Shared, live inbox
after.desc: Conversations update in real time with unread counts, profile photos, and search across names, numbers, and message text. Every reply shows which teammate sent it.

after.title: Assign & resolve
after.desc: Every conversation gets an owner and a status. Filter by Mine, Unassigned, or Resolved. Nothing slips through.

after.title: Tags & internal notes
after.desc: Label conversations your way ('vip', 'pedido', 'urgente') and leave private team notes the customer never sees.

after.title: Full history for everyone
after.desc: New teammate? They see the whole thread from day one. No handovers, no 'ask María what we told him'.

after.title: Roles that match your org
after.desc: Owners handle billing, admins manage numbers and webhooks, members work the inbox. Invite by email.

after.title: AI agent as first responder
after.desc: Optionally let an AI agent answer first and hand off to a human in the inbox when it's out of its depth.

after.title: More numbers as you grow
after.desc: Run support, sales, and ops on separate numbers. One inbox, filterable by number.

after.title: An API when you need it
after.desc: The same number is fully programmable: webhooks in, REST replies out. Your devs will thank you.

after.title: Per-member access
after.desc: Scope each teammate to specific numbers. Support sees the support line, sales sees sales. Owners see everything.

how.title: Scan a QR
how.desc: Connect your existing WhatsApp number from the dashboard. No Business API paperwork, no waiting.

how.title: Invite your team
how.desc: Send email invites and set roles: admins, members with per-number access, and operators who only see their assigned conversations.

how.title: Reply together
how.desc: The whole team answers from the browser. The phone stays in a drawer, connected and untouched.

teams.ctaTitle: Get the phone out of the workflow
teams.ctaSubtitle: Connect your number, invite the team, and answer WhatsApp like the rest of your tools. Together, from the browser.
teams.pricingSubtitle: Every plan includes the shared inbox. The tier sets how many of you can work it. Both start with a 7-day free trial.
